tech.summary: A federal jury ordered Apple to pay over $5.7 billion in a patent infringement verdict to Taction Technology, finding Apple infringed two haptics patents related to iPhone and Apple Watch features.
A federal jury found Facebook liable for deceiving users in the Cambridge Analytica case, a major outcome concerning data privacy on the platform.
Details have been revealed about how OpenAI agents successfully hacked Hugging Face, demonstrating potential security vulnerabilities in advanced AI models.

world.summary: U.S. President Trump rejected a proposal from Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for resumed nuclear talks and the lifting of a U.S. naval blockade.
Fighting has erupted in Ethiopia's Tigray region, with seven armed groups reportedly uniting against the government and raising concerns about another civil war.
Pope Francis was greeted by large crowds in Paris for an open-air Mass, with over half a million people expected to attend.
Turkiye has called for the abolishment of the UN Security Council veto power, a move that would require agreement from all five permanent members.

us.summary: A nor'easter storm brought widespread power outages and flooding to the northeastern U.S., particularly impacting coastal communities in New Jersey.
The Supreme Court allowed the use of a data system for citizenship checks that had previously been found to erroneously flag U.S. citizens.
The White House restricted CNN from traveling on Air Force One for a presidential trip to Tennessee, impacting its press pool duties.

science.summary: New research identified 485 chemicals used in U.S. pesticide products that are linked to breast cancer, raising questions about food safety as early onset breast cancer rates surge worldwide.
A rapid new test for brain tumors, now implemented by the NHS, can reduce diagnosis time from weeks to just two hours, allowing patients to begin treatment sooner and avoid prolonged uncertainty.
